title: AI-completed Beethoven Tenth Symphony premiered by the Beethoven Orchester Bonn on 9 October 2021
summary: AI-completed Beethoven Tenth premiered 9 Oct 2021 by Beethoven Orchester Bonn under Dirk Kaftan at the Telekom Forum, Bonn
account: On 9 October 2021 the Beethoven Orchester Bonn under Dirk Kaftan gave the world premiere at the Telekom Forum in Bonn of a Tenth Symphony completed with artificial intelligence, in a project funded by Deutsche Telekom, which organised the premiere, for Beethoven's 250th anniversary. Beethoven left only sketches for the work. A team led by musicologist Matthias Röder with AI researcher Ahmed Elgammal and Mark Gotham trained a model on Beethoven's output to generate continuations of the sketches; composer Walter Werzowa and musicologists chose and arranged the generated themes. Euronews reported on 13 October 2021 that the premiere had taken place in Bonn on 9 October. The benefit is a performed and recorded cultural artefact; the sources do not claim the result is Beethoven's.
purpose: Generate a completion of Beethoven's unfinished Tenth Symphony from his sketches in his style
system: Beethoven X AI generative music model (Elgammal/Playform AI team)
developer: Ahmed Elgammal (Rutgers University / Playform AI) with Mark Gotham
deployer: Deutsche Telekom (funder and concert organiser) with Beethoven Orchester Bonn

Small: one new performance and recording of a hypothetical completion; Euronews states humans chose and arranged the generated themes

ai_role.statement: The model generated candidate continuations of Beethoven's sketches; humans (Werzowa and the musicologists) selected, arranged and orchestrated them, so the AI contribution was generative input within a human-curated process. The vendor-side accounts (Elgammal in The Conversation; Telekom) and the orchestra's own programme page agree on the premiere.
